problem.text: Whether the constant function minimizes t(F,W) among nonnegative W with integral one, locally near the constant function, and inequalities between densities of signed graphons.

claims.text: Theorem 3.1: for every bipartite graph F with m edges, t(F,W) >= 1 whenever the integral of W is 1, 0 <= W <= 2 and the cut norm of W - 1 is at most 2^{-8m}. Theorem 3.2: the same with the Schatten-norm condition t(C_4, W - 1) <= 2^{-4m} (the statement prints t(C4, W); the sentence before it introduces t(C4, U)^{1/4} with U = W - 1). Theorem 3.3: the same in the L-infinity ball of radius 1/(4m). Theorem 3.4: t(F,W) >= 1 - epsilon without W <= 2, under a bound on densities of large sets. Lemma 2.22 bounds signed densities through the girth.

assumptions.text: Bounded measurable functions on the unit square; the analysis works with the signed function U = W - 1.

methods.text: Expansion of t(F, 1 + U) over spanning subgraphs; generalized Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities for signed graphons (Lemmas 2.3 to 2.6); hanging path systems; the girth lemma 2.22, whose proof treats separately the 1-subdivision of K_{3,3} through Lemma 2.5.

limitations.text: Only a neighbourhood of the constant function: small cut norm with W bounded by twice its mean, or small L-infinity norm. Removing the bound W <= 2 is open in the paper, which offers only the approximate Theorem 3.4.

relevance.text: The local results hold for every bipartite graph, so for every graph of girth at least six; they do not decide the statement. They give a necessary condition for a counterexample to the statement: the host W, scaled to mean one, has cut distance more than 2^{-8m} from the constant function or exceeds 2 on a set of positive measure, and has L-infinity distance more than 1/(4m) from it. In this paper the girth determines the order of the leading cycle term in the expansion (Lemma 2.22); it is not a hypothesis of the local theorem.
